conclusion: Yes, within the generated routed E22 FP32 fixture: growing shared training noise support from 2 to 8 seeds cut final held-out TEST RMSE 23.09%, 0.0533702454 to 0.0410462237, at 1,024 native updates per arm; all 11 preregistered gates passed. The eight-seed arm improved at all five fixed endpoints (896-1024), for every caption source and both held-out noise seeds, under both common frozen terminal critics; the TEST-minus-FIT MSE gap fell from 0.0005545459 to -0.0000674414, and zeroing its particle code raised RMSE to 0.0895439938. Both arms proposed 10 structural events and accepted zero, so this is a data-coverage effect, not a structural-controller mechanism. Limits: generated FP32 fixture with smaller dimensions than Supra; no Supra transfer tested; full-task LoRA RMSE 0.0633609846 still beats best particle 0.0679143351; no default adoption or Forge promotion. The variable is support size (228 vs 912 unique fit contexts), not a seed repeat.
hypothesis: Does growing the shared training noise support from 2 to 8 seeds improve unseen-noise conditional recovery when architecture, native game, initialization, updates and paired addresses are held fixed?
